candidates.summary: the changed-realm list is built from the uncapped Plan.ChangedRealms, so every changed realm the -max-realms cap dropped is posted as a working link and the cap note says the opposite
candidates.failure_scenario: A PR that touches more than 25 realm packages — a gnomod.toml or version sweep is the shape, and examples/gno.land/r has 58 of them. BuildPlan caps Plan.Realms at defaultMaxRealms=25 (pr-preview.yml passes no -max-realms) but never truncates Plan.ChangedRealms, and Crawler.Realms is plan.Realms, so only 25 realms are ever fetched or written. Comment then prints '**Changed realms (58)**' with 58 '- [`pkg`](base/r/...)' rows plus [source] and [help] per row: 33 of the 58 are 404s on the published preview, and the line under them reads '⚠️ 33 more affected realm(s) were not rendered (cap reached) — the changed realms are always kept.' The two other consumers of the same set filter on what was rendered — Index (comment.go:169, `if _, ok := c.pages[u]; !ok { continue }`) and ScreenshotPairs (shots.go:72, `head.FileOf` !ok -> continue) — so index.html and the screenshots show 25 realms while the comment claims 58. The same unfiltered write at comment.go:80 also links an indirect realm whose fetch returned non-200, which Crawler.Run skips silently (crawl.go:133).
candidates.verify_by: cp the artifact into misc/gnopreview and run `go test -run TestReachB5 -v ./...`: TestReachB5TreeWideChangeOutrunsTheCap feeds every examples/gno.land/r gnomod.toml as changed at the default cap, TestReachB5CommentLinksUnrenderedChangedRealms does it on the fake repo at cap 1
candidates.evidence: go1.25.9, misc/gnopreview at ecf7af0f2: 'changed files=58 ChangedRealms=58 Realms=25 Dropped=33 comment=16397 bytes' then '33 of 58 changed realms are linked by the comment but never rendered, e.g. [gno.land/r/gov/dao/treasury/test/v0 gno.land/r/gov/dao/treasury/v0 gno.land/r/nt/commondao/v0]'. On the fake repo at cap 1: 'comment links gno.land/r/x/lonely, which the cap dropped from the render set: https://example.test/pr-1/r/x/lonely/ 404s' and 'cap note claims every changed realm was kept, but 2 of 3 were dropped'.

candidates.summary: isSeed() drops every gnoweb seed realm from the affected list whenever Plan.Gnoweb is set, including seed realms the changed package genuinely affects, so a gnoweb+package PR can name no realm at all
candidates.failure_scenario: A PR touching gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/ and a p/ package imported only by seed realms — gno.land/p/leon/svgbtn/v0 is imported by r/gnoland/home and r/gnoland/boards2/v0, both in gnowebSeedRealms. BuildPlan returns Gnoweb=true, ChangedPkgs=[p/leon/svgbtn/v0], ChangedRealms empty, Realms=[the 4 seeds]; Mode() is 'both' so the default branch runs, and the indirect filter at line 69 excludes every seed because isSeed() cannot tell a realm BuildPlan appended as a seed from one already in Realms as a dependent (plan.go:264 appends only what is not already there and records nothing). The 'Realms affected through a changed package' section is therefore skipped entirely: the posted comment is the intro sentence, the homepage link and the sample screenshots, and it never names r/gnoland/home, r/gnoland/boards2/v0, or the changed package. With a mix of seed and non-seed dependents the section prints but its count understates and the affected seed realms are missing.
candidates.verify_by: `go test -run TestReachB5CommentHidesIndirectSeedRealm -v ./...` in misc/gnopreview with the artifact copied in: it builds the plan from the real tree and asserts every rendered realm is named in the comment
candidates.evidence: Mode="both" Gnoweb=true ChangedPkgs=[gno.land/p/leon/svgbtn/v0] Realms=[gno.land/r/docs/security_patterns gno.land/r/gnoland/blog gno.land/r/gnoland/boards2/v0 gno.land/r/gnoland/home], and the whole comment body is: marker, '### 🖼️ gnoweb preview', 'This PR changes **gnoweb** and realm sources. **[Open the preview homepage](...)**', then the <sub> footer — four failures, one per realm the comment never names.

candidates.summary: a plan that becomes empty leaves the previous preview comment standing, since no comment.md is written and the publish job treats a missing body as nothing to do
candidates.failure_scenario: Push 1 edits a realm: the preview renders and the comment is posted. Push 2 reverts that edit (the PR now touches docs only): render() returns at main.go:111 before Comment is ever called, so _preview/comment.md does not exist, and pr-preview-publish.yml:166 `[ -s _preview/comment.md ] || { echo "no comment body — nothing to post"; exit 0; }` exits before the PATCH at line 174. The PR keeps a preview comment listing realms the branch no longer touches, pointing at a snapshot of the old head. Comment()'s own empty-plan guard at line 24 is unreachable for the same reason — render() returns first — so the emptiness never reaches the publish path as an empty body either.
candidates.verify_by: read main.go:105-114 (early return before the comment.md write) against pr-preview-publish.yml:160-178; a run needs two pushes through the workflow
candidates.evidence: main.go:111 `if plan.Empty() { fmt.Println("nothing to preview"); return writeJSON(...preview.json, plan) }` — comment.md is written only at main.go:156; pr-preview-publish.yml:166 skips on a missing or empty body.
